newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: EU SEES BRATISLAVA AS KEY TO REGION'S DEVELOPMENT.
newsitem.headline: EU SEES BRATISLAVA AS KEY TO REGION'S DEVELOPMENT.

text.p: The European Union sees Slovakia's capital Bratislava as a key point for regional economic development, the EU's ambassador to Slovakia said on Wednesday.

"The Bratislava region is considered by the EU as one of the pilot regions for regional development and cross-border economic cooperation," Ambassador Georgios Zavvos told a news conference at a forum on Bratislava's economic development.
Bratislava is in a unique geographic position as the hub of three regions including Hungary's Gyor and Austria's Burgeland regions, Zavvos said.
"The EU current thinking is that this region which we call the 'golden triangle' is ideal for the development of regional and inter-regional development," Zavvos said.

According to a recent EU-sponsored study, the Bratislava region is ranked among the top ten production localities in western and eastern Europe considering its production costs, transport facilities, and infrastructure.
In the field of transport, the EU is financing studies on the development of rail, road and water transport networks between the three areas.

According to the study the level of wages in central and eastern European countries is exceptionally low compared to so-called "low labour cost" EC countries such as Portugal or the fast developing countries of the Far East.
For a country such as Slovakia to reach the same average wages as Portugal by the year 2020 labour costs would have to increase annually by some 34 percent, the study said.
